cards.text: This is a letter from Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the elect who are exiles scattered across Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia. Exiles, friend. Folks living far from home, and trust me, a stamper who spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer knows that feeling.

cards.question: Peter says these exiles were chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father. Who does he say sanctified them?

cards.text: Peter adds that this was for obedience to Jesus Christ and sprinkling by His blood. Then comes his greeting, and it's a generous one: "Grace and peace be yours in abundance."

cards.question: Peter bursts into praise: "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ!" He says that by His great mercy, God has given Peter and his readers new birth. Into what?
Peter says God has given this new birth into a living hope through the ___ of Jesus Christ from the dead.

cards.text: That same new birth is also into an inheritance. Now I'll be honest, friend, the closest I ever came to an inheritance was the 25-cent price sticker I went home with.

cards.question: True or false: Peter says this inheritance will slowly fade over time.

cards.text: Peter says that inheritance is imperishable, undefiled and unfading, reserved in heaven for them. Unfading, friend. I've got sprinkles that start fading the second they hit the counter.

cards.question: Peter says that through faith these believers are shielded by God's ___ for what is ready to be revealed in the last time.

cards.text: In all this they greatly rejoice. But Peter keeps it real: for a little while, they may have had to suffer grief in various trials.

Those trials prove the character of their faith, and Peter holds it up next to gold refined by fire. Friend, NOBODY has ever pulled raw dough out of the bowl and bragged about it, so I am not mad at a little heat.

cards.question: Peter says their proven faith is more precious than gold. True or false: he says gold perishes, even though it's refined by fire.
Peter says that proven faith may result in praise, glory and honor. When?

answers.text: At the revelation of Jesus Christ
At the end of their exile in Pontus
At the gathering of all the churches

cards.question: Peter's readers have not seen Jesus. True or false: Peter says they love Him anyway.
Peter's readers believe in Jesus without seeing Him, and they rejoice with an inexpressible and glorious joy. Peter says they're receiving the goal of their faith: the ___ of their souls.

cards.text: Then Peter looks back. The prophets who foretold this grace searched and investigated carefully, trying to figure out the time and setting the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing to.

cards.question: Peter says the Spirit of Christ in those prophets predicted two things about Christ. What were they?

answers.text: His sufferings and the glories to follow
His birth and His baptism in the river
His kingdom and the temple He would build

cards.text: And here's the twist. It was revealed to those prophets that all that work wasn't for themselves, and friend, I KNOW that one: you stamp cookies all day, and every crumb goes to somebody else's party.

cards.question: The prophets weren't serving themselves. Who does Peter say they were serving?
What the prophets foretold is now announced by those who preached the gospel by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. True or false: Peter says even angels long to look into these things.
